title: Sell Mineral Rights in Sheffield, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Sheffield, TX | Pecos County
metaDescription: Sheffield sits on the eastern edge of Pecos County near active Delaware Basin drilling. Get an honest valuation on your mineral or royalty interest.
heroLead: Sheffield is a tiny community along US-290 in eastern Pecos County, sitting close enough to the Reeves County line that the Delaware Basin's busier development has been reaching toward it.
intro: There isn't much to Sheffield itself, but its position matters more than its size. This part of Pecos County has seen horizontal Wolfcamp and Bone Spring activity extend in from the more heavily drilled acreage just across the county line, which is a real shift from the mostly older vertical production found farther west.

sections.heading: Eastern Pecos County, not western
paragraphs: The value picture in Pecos County differs sharply between its eastern and western halves, and Sheffield sits on the more active eastern side. If your family's minerals are near Sheffield, that generally supports a stronger current valuation than acreage farther southwest toward Fort Stockton.

sections.heading: Small-town title, same courthouse process
paragraphs: Even at Sheffield's small size, title work runs through the same Pecos County clerk's office in Fort Stockton as the rest of the county. Ranching-family inheritance is the common pattern here, and undivided interests split among heirs are typical rather than unusual.

sections.heading: What owners near the county line should watch for
paragraphs: Sitting this close to the Reeves County boundary means a tract technically mapped in Pecos County can be pooled into a unit that also draws from acreage across the line, or vice versa, depending on exactly how the spacing unit was drawn. It's not unusual for owners near Sheffield to be paid by an operator whose other units are mostly in Reeves County.

That cross-boundary pooling is a normal part of unconventional development and doesn't affect your ownership, but it's worth confirming which unit and which formation your specific interest is tied to before assuming what it's worth.

faqs.question: Is Sheffield in the more active part of Pecos County?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally. Eastern Pecos County near the Reeves County line has seen more horizontal development than the western half, and Sheffield sits in that eastern portion.

faqs.question: My family's interest near Sheffield hasn't been touched in a long time. Is it worth checking?
faqs.answer: Yes. Given the activity extending in from Reeves County, it's worth confirming current permits near your tract before assuming nothing's changed.

faqs.question: How do I start the process if I only have an old lease document?
faqs.answer: Send us what you have. We'll confirm the rest through Pecos County clerk records in Fort Stockton.

faqs.question: My check comes from an operator whose other wells seem to be in Reeves County. Is that normal for a Sheffield-area interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common near the county line, where spacing units sometimes draw from acreage on both sides. We'll confirm exactly which unit and formation your interest is tied to.
